The NavigationBar is used below 840 and the NavigationRail at 840 and above. Today, Timeline and Labs exist. Timeline and Labs show honest "Not built yet / Planned in Forge F003/F004" states. Today shows a specific empty weight state. The development and staging banner sits in the AppBar and is hidden in production, and tests cover it. There is no cloud, login, LLM or HTTP client code in lib/, and dart format on lib, test and integration_test exits 0. Required checks 1 to 7 exist in test/widget/shell_test.dart: renders at 4 sizes, Today at start, Timeline and Labs reached on both nav forms, phone gets nav-bar, desktop gets nav-rail, the screen changes. Gaps found: (1) The narrow layout has 4 primary destinations, because Medications is in kCompactPrimary. This breaks "exactly these primary destinations". (2) The wide rail shows all 10 doc-209 destinations as equal top-level items. The conflict between the kernel's "exactly Today/Timeline/Labs" and doc 209's 10 destinations is not recorded anywhere. (3) The Timeline placeholder always says "No records yet", even after a body-weight record is saved. (4) Required check 8 (starts without a network dependency) is only a partial static grep plus an assertion on a hard-coded label. flutter_test's mock HttpOverrides would let any HTTP call quietly return 400, and no Flutter test runs main() or bootstrap(). (5) The web smoke listens only for 'pageerror'. It does not capture console errors or failed or 4xx requests, which smoke step 4 requires. (6) No narrow-layout test navigates back to Today. (7) The web and Android display names are still the template name "human_health_os".

Read-only audit of human_health_os/lib/**, test/architecture/imports_test.dart, the storage policy tests, CI, packaging markers and the v0.32 kernel plus spec sections 2, 6-7 and 10-12. Nothing in lib/ shows fabricated or demo health values. No text claims a diagnosis, a recommendation, sync, or encryption that already exists. Capabilities are never shown as available because another platform has them. dart:io and dart:js_interop appear only in the two storage adapters, the domain layer is pure Dart, and --dart-define carries only the non-secret APP_ENV, APP_VERSION and SOURCE_REVISION. The EN and TR destination principles and banners say the same things. A web smoke receipt (reports/runtime/flutter_web_smoke.json) shows no external requests for the --no-web-resources-cdn build. There are two major findings. First, the F001 Timeline surface always says "No records yet", even when the vault holds saved body-weight records. Second, an unknown or absent APP_ENV falls back to the development profile, which is the only profile that writes plaintext, so a mistyped or flag-less release build persists unencrypted health data. The remaining findings are minor: capability and notice wording that blames the platform for a build-policy limit, a "no network calls" claim that depends on a build flag, gaps in the architecture guard, untranslated safety notices, stale Forge numbers for encryption, a banner whose disclaimer can be cut off, weight UI that ignores record fields, and lax handling of XDG paths and the version default. No finding is a blocker.

No blockers from this lens. The repository's gates are correct substitutes for the v0.32 literal commands.

Format gate. `dart format --help` on Dart 3.13.5 says `-o, --output [write] (default) Overwrite formatted files on disk`, so the literal `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` rewrites files. The repo already runs the read-only form `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed .` in CI line 48, CLAUDE.md line 28 and docs/TEST_STRATEGY.md line 9. Run now, it exits 0 (33 files visited, 0 changed).

Format scope. The CI scope `.` is safe. dart format skips hidden directories such as `.dart_tool`, `build/` holds no .dart files, and the 33 visited files are all under `lib/`, `test/` and `integration_test/`. So CI would not fail on generated files.

Web build. The literal `flutter build web` compiles here because the web SDK is cached. But the CDN flag defaults to true (`flutter_command.dart:811-816`), which embeds `FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit/<engine>/` (`web.dart:128-136`). That host is blocked here: `curl -I` returns `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`. So the literal build has a network dependency and would fail the smoke's "0 external requests" check and v0.32 required check 8. `--no-web-resources-cdn` (risk R-09) is the right equivalent, and CI, CLAUDE.md and the receipts all use it.

Receipt freshness. The receipt-backed gates at 9e86ed0 are still current for the app: `git diff 9e86ed0 HEAD -- human_health_os` is empty. CI has never run (the GitHub Actions API lists 0 workflow runs), and the state files say so.

The gaps are:
- The state self-audit does not enforce stale or dirty evidence.
- The untracked v0.32 spec will mark every new receipt dirty.
- The web smoke does not capture console errors.
- `flutter doctor -v` is absent from CI and CLAUDE.md, and the existing doctor report is stale.
- The command substitutions are not recorded as v0.32 deviations, and two docs still show the old commands.
- The gate sets in CI and CLAUDE.md differ, including `--enforce-lockfile`.
- The runtime receipt does not bind to the build it tested, and the smoke and receipt disagree on the dirty flag.
